C005.subject: Free trade agreements
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Free trade agreements export-oriented industries in Southeast Asia]

[PATH:empirical] World Bank Enterprise Surveys for Southeast Asian countries (e.g., Vietnam, Thailand, Indonesia) analyzing firm-level R&D spending and patenting activity before and after FTA implementation — Provides quantitative firm-level data on innovation inputs and outputs in export-oriented industries, enabling difference-in-differences or panel regression analysis to test causal effect of FTAs.

[PATH:literature] Case studies of technology transfer clauses in specific FTAs (e.g., ASEAN-Australia-New Zealand FTA, CPTPP) and their impact on local supplier upgrading in electronics or automotive sectors — Allows qualitative assessment of mechanisms linking FTA provisions (e.g., intellectual property, investment rules) to innovation adoption in export-oriented firms, complementing quantitative findings.

[PATH:empirical] Patent data from the ASEAN Patent Examination Cooperation (ASPEC) or USPTO filings by Southeast Asian firms in export-oriented sectors, matched with FTA timeline — Directly measures technological innovation via patent counts and citations, enabling event study or synthetic control methods to isolate FTA effects from other global trends.

C006.subject: Free trade
C006.predicate: undermines local industrialization and traps developing economies in low-value commodity production
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Free trade developing economies]

[PATH:empirical] Comparative case studies of manufacturing sectors in Sub-Saharan Africa vs. East Asia post-1980s trade liberalization — Directly tests whether free trade led to deindustrialization in Sub-Saharan Africa and Latin America relative to East Asian economies that pursued selective protectionism, controlling for initial conditions and policy differences.

[PATH:empirical] Longitudinal panel data on export complexity and value-added in developing economies (e.g., UNCTAD's export sophistication index) correlated with tariff reduction timelines — Quantifies whether free trade periods are associated with stagnation or decline in export sophistication, indicating a trap in low-value commodity production.

[PATH:theoretical] New structural economics and dependency theory literature (e.g., Chang, 2002; Rodrik, 2016) on the historical role of infant industry protection in industrialization — Provides theoretical grounding for the causal mechanism linking free trade to underindustrialization, and identifies counterarguments from comparative advantage theory.

qualifier.geographic: Sub-Saharan Africa and parts of Latin America

C007.subject: Free trade
C007.predicate: accelerates urbanization and diminishes rural livelihoods
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Free trade developing economies]

[PATH:empirical] World Bank Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS) panel data for Sub-Saharan Africa (post-2000) — Provides longitudinal household-level data on rural income, employment, and migration patterns, enabling direct testing of whether trade liberalization correlates with urbanization and decline in rural livelihoods.

[PATH:empirical] National Sample Survey (NSS) employment-unemployment data from India (post-2000) combined with trade policy variation across Indian states — Allows quasi-experimental analysis of differential exposure to free trade reforms on rural-to-urban migration and informal sector outcomes in South Asia, leveraging state-level variation.

[PATH:literature] Meta-analysis of trade liberalization and rural welfare in developing economies (e.g., journal articles from Journal of Development Economics or World Development) — Synthesizes existing empirical findings to assess overall direction and magnitude of effects, identifying conditions under which the hypothesis holds or fails, and gaps in current evidence.

C008.subject: Free trade
C008.predicate: reduces income inequality and strengthens local subsistence agriculture
evidence_refs: [Simulated evidence for: Free trade developing economies]

[PATH:empirical] Household-level panel data from the Living Standards Measurement Study (LSMS) for Sub-Saharan African countries (e.g., Ethiopia, Uganda, Malawi) covering post-2000 trade liberalization periods, combined with tariff reduction schedules from the World Bank's World Integrated Trade Solution (WITS) database. — This source allows testing whether tariff reductions correlate with changes in income distribution and subsistence agriculture output at the household level, directly addressing the disputed causal claim within the specified geographic and temporal scope.

[PATH:literature] Systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on trade liberalization and agricultural outcomes in low-income countries, focusing on informal and subsistence sectors, such as those cataloged in the Campbell Collaboration or 3ie Development Evidence Portal. — A meta-analysis synthesizes existing evidence from multiple contexts to assess the overall direction and strength of the relationship, helping to resolve the disputed status by identifying consistent patterns or heterogeneity across Sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia.

[PATH:theoretical] Computable General Equilibrium (CGE) models calibrated for Sub-Saharan African and South Asian economies, incorporating detailed representation of rural subsistence agriculture and informal labor markets, with simulations of post-2000 trade liberalization scenarios. — CGE models provide a theoretical framework to isolate the mechanisms through which free trade might reduce inequality and strengthen subsistence agriculture, testing the hypothesis under controlled assumptions and identifying necessary conditions for the predicted effects.
